topIssues.title: kona-node: accept base64-encoded custom L1 chain configs
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Problem

Custom-L1 deployments may inject the L1 genesis through `KONA_NODE_L1_CHAIN_CONFIG` as base64-encoded JSON. `kona-node` currently parses that environment value as a `PathBuf` and calls `File::open`, so sufficiently large configs fail at startup with:

```
Error: Failed to open l1 config file: File name too long (os error 36)
```

This was observed with a netchef-managed custom-L1 devnet. The encoded genesis was about 52 KB and never reached JSON parsing.

## Proposed behavior

Keep accepting a file path, but fall back to standard base64-encoded JSON when the configured value is not a readable file. Support both forms already documented for custom L1 configuration:

- a directly encoded L1 chain config
- a genesis document with the L1 chain config under `.config`

Add unit coverage for file and base64 inputs so custom-L1 deployments do not regress.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Default-`X` benchmarking
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: `X` (the offset between the chosen L1 anchor's timestamp and the committed L2 `genesis_time`) must be large enough that `genesis_time` is still in the future when `OPCM.deploy()` is mined; otherwise `op-node` will produce empty filler blocks at L2 block time to fill the gap. Measure end-to-end runtime of the off-chain portion of the pipeline (anchor selection through prestate generation) against a real prestate builder, repeated enough times to get a stable result. Propose a default `X`.

topPRs.title: op-script-engine: Rust forge-script executor + Go client and parity gates
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Rust `op-script-engine` crate + Go client and byte-parity gates — the base of the op-geth-decoupling script-engine stack (epic #20257 §16). **Additive: no production code selects this engine yet.**

Stack (each stacked on the previous):
1. **this PR** — engine crate, `rustengine` client, parity gates
2. non-forked op-deployer routing + engine default (follows)
3. fork-mode routing + boundary deletion (follows)

### Contents
- **`rust/op-script-engine`** — revm-based re-implementation of the `op-chain-ops/script` EVM host: a cheatcode + console `Inspector`, prank/broadcast capture, forge-artifact loader, state dump, the OPCM `RunScript*` input/output-precompile mechanism, and an RPC-backed fork mode. Served over a UDS JSON-RPC transport (reth-ipc + jsonrpsee).
- **`op-chain-ops/script/rustengine`** — Go client plus A/B parity tests that drive both the Go host and this engine and assert **byte-identical** output: state-dump + broadcast (incl. `gasUsed`), OPCM `RunScriptSingle`/`Void`, and forked `SetDisputeGameImpl` over a hermetic recorded-RPC fixture.
- **Additive helpers** the parity path needs: `script.Precompile` snapshot reflection, `script.Host.ExportDiff`, and a `forking.AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref fix. `go-tests` provisions the workspace-built binary so the gates run in CI.

### Gates (local)
- `cargo test -p op-script-engine` — 16/16
- `cargo clippy -p op-script-engine --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; nightly `fmt` clean
- `go test ./op-chain-ops/script/rustengine/` — parity / OPCM / forked / isolated-fork all pass
- base goldens (`TestScriptStateDump|TestScriptBroadcast`) and `./op-chain-ops/script/forking/` unchanged-green

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Review batch applied
Crate hardening (all byte-parity re-validated): contained worker-thread panics (`catch_unwind`); standard precompiles `0x01..=0x0a` no longer framed/broadcast-captured (matches the Go host, which frames only bytecode-bearing targets); `tx.chain_id: None` on raw calls (matches geth's `EVM.Call`, fixes a stale-id case after `vm.chainId`); host setters record into the fork diff when forked; documented that `isolate_broadcast`'s `transaction_id` bump also re-baselines SSTORE originals (revm's cold-slot reset == geth `Finalise(true)`).

Go client hardening: stderr drain uses `bufio.Reader` (no 64KiB line-cap hang); Linux `Pdeathsig=SIGKILL` so a hard-killed test can't leak engines. Test rigor: `TestMain`→`ProvisionTestBinary` + a `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE` guard so the byte-parity gate can't silently skip; a targeted `AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref regression test; non-vacuity guards on the parity subtests.

**Two flagged potential divergences investigated — both non-divergences:** the implemented cheatcode set is complete for the OPCM-routed scripts (env*/toString/parseJson/file-IO are used only by the legacy forge scripts, never routed; verified by the passing full-suite A/B gates), and the isolated-broadcast SSTORE-original re-baseline is handled by revm (source-confirmed).

**One real divergence found — access control:** enforcing Go's cheatcode access control naively breaks byte parity, because the routed deploy scripts deploy helper contracts that call cheatcodes and rely on Go's transitive auto-grant-on-deploy. Left **unenforced** (the current byte-parity-correct behavior, documented in `cheatcodes.rs`); correct enforcement needs the auto-grant replicated and is a dedicated follow-up.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: delete the Go script engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**CLI break:** the `--script-engine` / `DEPLOYER_SCRIPT_ENGINE` flag is gone (on `op-deployer apply`, `bootstrap`, `inspect l2-semvers`, `manage`, `upgrade`, and `op-fetcher`). It never shipped in a released `op-deployer`; with one engine there is nothing to select.

**Cross-repo compile break:** deleting `scriptbackend.FromHost` and the `FetchChainInfo(*script.Host, …)` signature (now only `FetchChainInfoWithBackend(scriptbackend.Backend, …)`) breaks the external superchain-registry `ops` module the next time it bumps its `optimism` pin past this commit. It is deliberate — the Go host is gone — but needs a coordinated downstream update (switch the caller to `FetchChainInfoWithBackend`).

Deletes the Go script engine so the Rust `op-script-engine` is the only implementation. This lets `op-chain-ops/script` drop every geth `core/vm | state | trie | triedb | tracers | ethdb` import — the blocker for depending on upstream go-ethereum (§16 of #20257).

Three commits:
1. **goldenize** — record the live Go host's outputs (allocs JSON, broadcast lists, fork diffs) from the base tip as committed fixtures and convert every A/B parity gate into a Rust-vs-fixture golden regression test. The safety net survives the host's deletion. CI arms it: the go-test jobs set `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` so a missing engine binary fails the golden gates loudly instead of skipping the sole post-deletion proof of the Go host's behavior.
2. **delete** — remove the in-process geth-EVM host machinery in `op-chain-ops/script` (host EVM, cheatcode precompile dispatch, prank machinery), `op-chain-ops/script/forking` (~2088 LOC RPC ForkDB), the Go arms behind the flag, and Go-only host tests. Tests that constructed Go forked hosts are migrated to the Rust engine or deleted with written rationale.
3. **flag removal** — delete the `op-deployer/pkg/env` script-engine package and the flag/param plumbing (`scriptbackend.NewForkedL1`, `interopgen.Deploy`, the interopgen host factory).

Kept (the Rust path depends on them): `script.Context`, Broadcast types + JSON, the foundry artifacts packages, the Precompile reflection machinery, ABI helpers, `DeployScript` wrappers, the `rustengine` package.

Local sweep green: `go test ./op-chain-ops/...`, the goldens (L2Genesis 5 modes, pipeline L1/L2, 9 forks, semvers, interopgen, rustengine, scriptbackend) run under `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` with the pre-built binary, `op-e2e/config`, `op-e2e/interop TestInteropDevRecipe`, `cargo test -p op-script-engine`. Remaining `./op-deployer/...` failures are pre-existing environmental gates (network `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`, forge recompile, a missing local artifact) that also fail on the base and do not reach any changed code.

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: op-deployer: default non-forked script execution to the Rust engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Routes op-deployer's **non-forked** script execution through the Rust `op-script-engine` by default; `--script-engine=go` falls back to the in-process Go host. Part 2 of the op-geth-decoupling script-engine stack (epic #20257 §16).

**Stacked on #21750** — review/merge that first. Base of this PR is `seb/script-engine-core`.

### What routes to the engine
- L2Genesis stage, L1 genesis deploy stages, `op-chain-ops/interopgen`, and `inspect l2-semvers`.
- Forked hosts (apply Live/Calldata, bootstrap, upgrade, manage, sysgo) **stay on the Go host** behind an explicit, commented per-host-kind boundary. Fork-mode routing is the next PR.

### How
- `env.ScriptEngineKind` (`go`|`rust`, default `rust`) + the `--script-engine` flag.
- Per-operation seam: `pipeline.NewEngineScripts` + `Env.L1Engine` route each L1/L2 deploy op to the engine or the Go host; interopgen gains a `DeployHost` seam; `inspect.L2Semvers` gains a reader seam.

### Parity (local gates, all green)
- `TestL2GenesisAllocsInvariants` — now runs on the Rust engine by default.
- A/B byte-parity vs the Go host: L1+L2 pipeline (5 alloc modes), L2Genesis, the op-e2e fork range, interopgen (L1 + 2×L2), l2-semvers, op-e2e genesis smoke.
- No regression: base goldens, `env` unit tests. `go build ./op-e2e/... ./op-devstack/...` clean; gofmt/vet clean.
- CI provisions the workspace-built binary for the fault-proof-deps and sysgo (acceptance) jobs.

**No forge-based deployment change.** The Go host remains the `--script-engine=go` fallback.

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### ⚠️ New runtime dependency (packaging note for release)
Because non-forked genesis now defaults to the Rust engine, a released `op-deployer apply --deployment-target genesis` (and `inspect l2-semvers`) needs the `op-script-engine` binary available at runtime. `--script-engine=go` restores the fully in-process path. Live/Calldata targets are unaffected in this PR (they stay forked→Go until the next PR of the stack).

### Review batch applied
- The genesis engine selection is now an **exhaustive switch** with a loud default (matching `pipeline.GenerateL2Genesis` / `inspect.L2Semvers`), so an unrecognized kind never silently falls back to Go.
- `TestMain`→`ProvisionTestBinary` added to `op-e2e/config` and `op-e2e/interop` so their genesis tests (now on the Rust default) resolve the binary locally without a manual pre-build (CI already exports it). The broader `op-e2e/system/*` subpackages are CI-covered; a per-package TestMain is a follow-up if local runs are wanted.
- `.circleci` unchanged this batch; `merge-configs.sh` re-validated (exit 0).

### op-deployer image build fix — rustbin relocated to op-service
The op-deployer Docker image's Go build stage failed under `-mod=readonly`: production `op-deployer` transitively imported `op-devstack/shared/rustbin` (system-test infra, which also drags in an op-challenger subtree) through `op-chain-ops/script/rustengine/binary.go`. Single `go.mod`, so the failure is that subtree, not a missing directory.

Fixed by **relocating** the generic Rust-binary provisioner (`Spec`/`EnsureExists`, op-service-only deps) to `op-service/rustbin` (`git mv`) and repointing its 7 `Spec`-consumers (binary.go + sysgo op_rbuilder/rollup_boost/runtime_state/mixed_runtime + shared/challenger + op-e2e reth). The op-challenger-dependent kona-host oracle runner (`kona_host_native.go`, uses no `Spec`) stays in `op-devstack/shared/rustbin`. This inverts the production→test-infra import edge. Verified: `go list -deps ./op-deployer/...` now has **zero op-devstack**; whole-module `go build ./...` green. (Docker image itself pending the CI build-images verification.)

_Follow-up (cosmetic, not this PR): the `op-devstack/shared/rustbin` remnant now holds only the kona-host oracle runner — rename to `op-devstack/shared/konahost` when convenient._

---

### Release packaging — RESOLVED: op-deployer bundles + auto-resolves the engine
The runtime dependency above is now satisfied with **no change to op-deployer's external API** — no new env var, flag, or path for users.

- **Resolution (`rustengine.EngineBinary`):** lookup order is now `RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_SCRIPT_ENGINE` override → **op-script-engine adjacent to the running executable** → rust/target discovery. The adjacency rule makes both the Docker image and any release archive work with zero configuration. Nothing resolving stays a loud error. (`--script-engine=go` is unchanged; the env override still works.) Covered by `TestAdjacentEngineBinary`.
- **Docker:** the op-deployer image now builds op-script-engine in an alpine (musl) Rust stage and places it next to `op-deployer` in `/usr/local/bin` (`ops/docker/op-stack-go/Dockerfile`). ⚠️ **Not verifiable in my environment** (no buildx + broken Docker bridge networking here) — needs a CI/infra image build to confirm the musl multi-arch compile. **Design decision for infra:** this compiles op-script-engine (revm/alloy/ring) inline in every op-deployer image build (×2 arches, arm64 emulated) — a real build-time cost. The alternative is a separate cached/pinned op-script-engine image `COPY --from`'d in (the cannon pattern). I implemented the inline version as a concrete starting point; flag if you'd prefer the separate image.
- **Release archives:** goreleaser doesn't build Rust, so the engine can't be dropped into the archives without a Rust cross-compile matrix (linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64; darwin/windows need osxcross/mingw). `op-deployer/.goreleaser.yaml` documents the exact `archives.files` entry to uncomment once the release pipeline stages the per-platform binaries.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: add proposer L1 query ports
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Introduce crate-private `L1View` and `QueryTime` ports for proposer observations.
- Add production adapters backed by the existing Alloy provider and contracts.
- Make `Proposer` non-generic while preserving its public constructor and policy behavior.
- Add focused characterization tests for read boundaries, failure isolation, and time handling.

## Why

This is the first in a series of changes that create independently controllable boundaries around the proposer’s external dependencies. These boundaries will enable deterministic scenario tests for complex lifecycle, failure, timing, and concurrency behavior without requiring live L1 infrastructure or real proofs.

Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22171
